sources.fact: The Kahun Gynaecological Papyrus, the oldest known Egyptian medical text (c. 1825 BC), describes a contraception method using crocodile dung; whether it was burned/sprinkled or inserted is debated
Kahun papyrus around 1825 BC, famous for crocodile dung contraception; how it was meant to be used is a matter of debate
Condoms are up to 98% effective at preventing pregnancy if used correctly every time; condoms protect against HIV and other STIs

math.note: years since c. 1825 BC, so 'almost 4,000 years ago'

post.instagram_caption:
Ancient Egypt had... interesting ideas about birth control 🐊

The Kahun papyrus, written around 1825 BC, lists crocodile dung as a contraceptive. Historians still argue about how it was used, and there is no evidence it worked.

Today condoms are up to 98% effective when used correctly, and they also help protect against STIs.

Sources: Kahun Gynaecological Papyrus, NHS.
